## Curated samples

| Analysis | Records | Females | Seasons |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Clutch size | 12,627 | 8,894 | 44 |
| Egg-to-fledging success | 9,790 | 7,132 | 39 |

Egg-to-fledging success is the number of fledglings in a brood divided by its initial clutch size (the number of eggs laid), representing the proportion of eggs that produced a fledgling. Throughout the analyses, “fledging success” is shorthand for this egg-based measure.

[Input files and loading code](workflow.qmd)

## Predictor definitions

Relative laying date is first-egg date minus the within-season median. Female age is yearling or older; continuous year and temperature are centred. `year_f` identifies the random-effect groups.

<details class="analysis-code">
<summary>Show R code</summary>

```r
# Inspect the columns actually supplied to the fitted model.
d <- read.csv("data_derived/analysis/clutch_model_data.csv")
d$age_class <- factor(d$age_class, levels = c("YOUNG", "OLD"))
d$year_f <- factor(d$year_f)
str(d)
summary(d)
levels(d$age_class)
table(d$year_f)
```

</details>

::: {.callout-note .review-summary appearance="simple"}

## Retained checks

- Clutch predictor VIFs: temperature 1.21; year 1.22.
- Fledging VIFs: relative date 1.046; age 1.055; temperature 1.267; year 1.269.
- Individual-window and female-specific thermal-slope extensions did not yield admissible fits; they are not used for inference.

The original raw-data cleaning history is not included; these pages start from the [public curated model-ready files](data_derived/analysis/README.md).
